Subject: Partner: artifact handover patterns for SOC2 evidence (SecPulse <> Redwood)

Hi Mina / Kimberly,

Nice to meet you — I’m Danielle on the partnerships team at SecPulse. We’re starting intake work to connect our GRC evidence broker to Redwood’s artifact store. Before we schedule engineering time, a couple quick clarifying questions so we can scope effort and compliance artifacts appropriately:

- Preferred transfer mechanism: S3 presigned URLs (short-lived) vs SFTP drop vs secure HTTPS POST? We assume S3 presigned is easiest for large archives but want to confirm.
- Manifest format: do you prefer a JSON manifest with SHA256 checksums or a CSV? Any schema constraints for the manifest (metadata fields we must include)?
- Redaction: some artifacts include redacted user identifiers. Do you require a specific redaction tokenization pattern, or is a redaction flag in the manifest sufficient?
- Retention & deletion: for onboarding SOC2 evidence we assume 90-day retention with a one-time archival to customer-managed bucket if requested. Confirm.

I’ve attached a first-pass handover spec and a short transfer checklist (see attachments). If these answers look straightforward, can we book a 30-min sync with your engineering/assurance lead next week?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

— Danielle

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Partner: artifact handover patterns for SOC2 evidence (SecPulse <> Redwood)

Hi Danielle — thanks for the clear deck and checklist. High-level answers below; happy to chat after you’ve reviewed.

- Transfer mechanism: presigned S3 URLs are our preferred path for production evidence ingests. They work well with large archives and allow us to enforce short TTLs and tight IAM scoping. For initial proof-of-concept we can accept HTTPS POSTs to a temporary intake endpoint if you need to avoid S3 setup, but that would be treated as a lower-throughput path.

- Manifest format: JSON manifest with an array of objects is preferable. Required fields: filename, size_bytes, sha256, artifact_type (log,config,screenshot), evidence_date, redaction_flag (true/false). Optional: original_path, customer_request_id.

- Redaction: a redaction_flag in the manifest is fine. If the artifact contains PII, we require a short description of redaction method (e.g., tokenized_email / hashed_ip) included in manifest.redaction_method. We can accept hashed tokens but ask you to avoid reversible encodings.

- Retention: 90 days default for staging bucket, with optional archival to customer-managed S3 for longer retention on request. Deletion requests should be submitted via the HubSpot deal or a signed request; we’ll follow the retention SLA in the contract.

Next steps: can you share which internal SecPulse product team will be owning the transfer (engineer contact)? I’ll loop in Marcus Lin (platform integrations) to scope the runbook. If you can do a 30-min meeting Tues or Wed next week, propose times and we’ll lock it.

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
